title: SSR Integration with Next.js
description: Learn how to integrate React Query with Next.js SSR and SSG for optimal server-side data fetching.

data.text: Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and Static Site Generation (SSG) allow you to fetch data on the server before sending HTML to the client. React Query integrates seamlessly with these patterns through `dehydrate` and `hydrate`, giving you the best of both worlds: server-rendered HTML and client-side caching.

React Query is designed for client-side data fetching. When you move fetching to the server, you face a new challenge: how do you transfer server-fetched data to the client cache so that `useQuery` does not refetch data that is already fresh? The answer is `dehydrate` and `hydrate`.

data.title: Why Not Just Use Server Components Directly?
data.text: Server Components can fetch data without React Query. However, using React Query on the server gives you caching, deduplication, and a unified API between server and client. This is especially valuable when the same data is needed in both contexts.

`dehydrate` serializes the QueryClient cache into a format that can be embedded in your HTML. On the client, `hydrate` restores the cache from that serialized data. Together, they ensure the client starts with the same data the server fetched, eliminating duplicate requests.

data.caption: SSR data flow with React Query dehydrate and hydrate
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Server
    participant Q as QueryClient
    participant H as HydrationBoundary
    participant C as Client

    S->>Q: Create new QueryClient
    S->>Q: prefetchQuery(key, fn)
    Q->>S: Data fetched and cached
    S->>S: dehydrate(queryClient)
    S->>C: Send HTML + serialized cache
    C->>H: Restore cache state
    H->>C: useQuery reads from hydrated cache
    C->>C: No refetch needed (data is fresh)

data.title: QueryClient Lifecycle
data.text: Create a new QueryClient for every SSR request. Do not reuse a single QueryClient across requests, as this causes cache leakage between users.

In Next.js App Router, Server Components can fetch data directly. You can prefetch queries inside a Server Component and pass the dehydrated state to a Client Component boundary. This pattern keeps your data fetching close to where it is consumed while still leveraging React Query's caching.

data.text: A hydration mismatch occurs when the server-rendered HTML differs from the initial client render. React Query's `hydrate` function prevents this by ensuring the client cache is populated before the first render. However, you must avoid accessing browser-only APIs like `window` or `localStorage` during the initial server render.

terms.definition: Serializes the QueryClient cache into a JSON-safe format for embedding in HTML.
Restores a serialized cache into the client-side QueryClient.
A React Query component that marks the boundary where client-side cache hydration occurs.

data.title: Client-Only Code
data.text: Any code that accesses `window`, `document`, or `localStorage` must be inside a `'use client'` component with proper guards or loaded dynamically to prevent SSR errors.

data.title: Set Up SSR with a Profile Page
data.description: Create a Next.js Server Component that prefetches a user profile using React Query and hydrates it in a Client Component.
steps: Create a new page at app/users/[id]/page.tsx as a Server Component
Instantiate a new QueryClient inside the page function
Call prefetchQuery with the user query key and a fetchUser function
Wrap the Client Component in HydrationBoundary with dehydrate(queryClient)
In the Client Component, call useQuery with the same query key
Verify in the Network tab that no duplicate request is made on hydration
data.expectedOutcome: Server renders the user data, client hydrates the cache, and no duplicate fetch occurs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: dehydrate serializes the cache for HTML embedding
hydrate restores the cache on the client
Create a new QueryClient per SSR request
Avoid browser APIs during server rendering
data.takeaway: SSR with React Query eliminates duplicate requests and provides instant first paints.
